relevance_note: Paediatric HA20 cohort with per-patient tables: "17 patients from 11 unrelated families, with disease onset before 18 years of age and carrying a tumour necrosis factor alpha-induced protein 3 (TNFAIP3) mutation, were included."
method_note: A Python script in the scratch directory transcribed Table 3 (variants per patient/family) and supplementary tables 1a (demographics, onset and disease-course features), 1b (laboratory) and 1c (treatments), in which patients are columns headed P1-P17; the script quotes each row from its row label through that patient's cell, and its output was spot-checked against the tables. Labels use the text's form 'patient N' (supplementary tables print P1-P17). Supplementary table 1a 'Present'/'Absent' were read as stated presence/absence; onset and disease-course rows are separate phenotypic_features rows (phase in severity_or_detail). Several patients have a feature present at onset but 'Absent' in the disease-course row (e.g. patient 6 and 7 fever, patient 7 skin eruption); this was treated as a change over time, not a contradiction, and the checklist item is observed. Checklist mapping: 'Fever' was mapped to 'recurrent fever'; 'Skin eruption' Absent in both phases excludes the skin-lesion item; arthritis-or-arthralgia is excluded only when all four arthritis/arthralgia rows are Absent; Absent for uveitis, lymphadenopathy, pericarditis, colitis and headache does not exclude the broader checklist items. Table 1b: '+/-' and 'yes/no' and 'neg' are defined in its legend (quoted as a second span); '/' is not available; DSDNA '0' (P7), Hyper IgM '1' (P15) and numeric values (CRP, ESR, calprotectin, SAA, interferon) were not interpreted, so 'elevated inflammatory markers' is not reported for everyone. Table 1c 'X' (P17 etanercept effectiveness) was not interpreted. Treatment spans were merged into contiguous table blocks to keep within five spans; patient 7's Kawasaki treatment did not fit and is left out of treatment_summary. Table 3's 'Reference(s)' column cites the variant's prior reports (e.g. 'Not published'), not the patient, so it was not copied into source_reference_in_review; only patient 16 has a source reference (El Khouri et al^44). No zygosity statement exists; zygosity is not reported. Variant type 'nonsense' comes from the sentence calling p. Arg87*, p. Arg183* and p. Trp164* 'stop-gain'. Patient 14's complex allele c. [29T>A; 49A>T] is one row. The ACMG codes (PVS1 + PM2) are given for the two novel mutations (patients 6 and 14). Relatives: family 2 (patient 4's mother, grandfather, an aunt and two nieces of the grandfather, and 'another cousin', labelled 'unnamed person 1' because the text does not say whose cousin) and family 8 (patient 10's half-brother, half-sister, mother and maternal grandfather) are described in the text. Table 3 lists patients 10-13 as family 8, so the family 8 relatives very probably are patients 11-13 (e.g. the mother's uveitis and patient 12's uveitis), but the paper never states the mapping, so they were NOT merged and may duplicate study patients. The aunt and nieces were 'reported to have recurrent ulcers and chronic hepatitis' collectively; no per-person features were recorded for them. No variant rows were made for relatives except patient 17's asymptomatic parent, who carries 'the same variant'. The pedigree and treatment-timeline figures (supplementary figures 1 and 2) lost their layout in conversion and were not used. Contradictions: ANA is '+' for 8 of 14 tested in supplementary table 1b but the text says 7/13; hyper IgA 'yes' 4 of 13 vs text 3/11; hypergammaglobulinaemia 'yes' 3 of 13 vs text 4/11. Patient 1: text says 'mildly elevated faecal calprotectin' but table 1b gives 'neg' during flares (both rows emitted). Group statements 'No patient fulfilled ... connective tissue disease or isolated juvenile idiopathic arthritis' and 'No cases of SLE' exclude those for all 17 patients (inferred from group statement). Clinical diagnosis basis comes from 'All patients carried a pathogenic or likely pathogenic TNFAIP3 variant.'
